close_reason: Updated jmap-filenode-client README: client sends one HTTP request regardless of depth; O(depth) backend calls are server-side. Updated jmap-filenode-server README: added Known Limitations bullet describing default O(depth) query_subtree behavior and override path.
description:
The jmap-filenode-client README Known Limitations section currently states:

'file_node_query with depth > 0 issues one FileNode/query request per level; for deep trees this is O(depth) round-trips, not a single recursive server query.'

This is incorrect. The client sends exactly ONE HTTP request to the JMAP server, with the depth integer included as a JSON field in the request body. The O(depth) backend calls are made by the SERVER handler (jmap-filenode-server) internally as it calls query_objects per level against its storage backend — the client has no visibility into this.

Fix: Update the Known Limitations bullet to accurately describe what the client does (one request) vs what the server handler does internally (N backend calls). Point readers at jmap-filenode-server if they want to understand or optimize the server-side behavior.

Also update jmap-filenode-server README to add a corresponding Known Limitations bullet describing the O(depth) backend calls and pointing at JMAP-[filenode query_subtree bead] as the tracking issue.

Acceptance criteria:
- jmap-filenode-client README accurately describes one HTTP request for any depth value
- jmap-filenode-server README mentions O(depth) backend calls and the query_subtree improvement path
- No code changes
title: jmap-filenode-client: Correct README — depth sends one HTTP request, not O(depth)
